Thermal imaging with CWSI supports timing and zoning of irrigation; fusion with multispectral data
separates heat and nutrient stress (Jackson et al., 1981; Berni et al., 2009; Deery et al., 2016; Ndlovu et al.,
2024).

links.passage:
Deep models detect and grade infections (e.g., late blight, rust) before canopy-wide symptoms, enabling
targeted responses (Mohanty et al., 2016; Polder et al., 2019; Ashurov et al., 2024; Radočaj et al., 2025).
supporting_passages:
Drones (unmanned aerial vehicles, UAVs) have rapidly transitioned from experimental tools to
 dependable, field-scale systems for crop health monitoring. By delivering on-demand, centimeter-level
 imagery and thermal/structural measurements, UAVs enable early diagnosis of nutrient limitations,
 water stress, pest and disease outbreaks, and stand establishment issues.
links.inference_note: The abstract establishes that the deep models operate on UAV imagery, and the 6.3 passage states that this early detection enables targeted responses to disease.
links.citation_in_text: Mohanty et al., 2016; Polder et al., 2019; Ashurov et al., 2024; Radočaj et al., 2025
reference_entries: 25. Mohanty, S.P., et al. (2016). Using Deep Learning for Plant Disease. Frontiers in Plant Science.
26. Polder, G., et al. (2019). Detection of Late Blight in Potato from UAV. Remote Sensing.
9. Ashurov, A.Y., et al. (2024). Enhancing Plant Disease Detection through Deep Learning. Frontiers in Plant Science.
7. Radočaj, D., et al. (2025). Evolution of Deep Learning in UAV-Based Crop Disease Detection. Applied Sciences.

links.passage:
High-resolution RGB/MS supports inter-row weed detection and site-specific control, reducing herbicide
loads and drift (Peña et al., 2015; Louargant et al., 2018; Lottes et al., 2017).
links.citation_in_text: Peña et al., 2015; Louargant et al., 2018; Lottes et al., 2017
reference_entries: 27. Peña, J.M., et al. (2015). Weed Mapping in Sunflower Using UAV Imagery. Remote Sensing.
28. Louargant, M., et al. (2018). Weed Detection in Rapeseed Using UAV RGB. Precision Agriculture.
29. Lottes, P., et al. (2017). Weed Detection for Precision Farming. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters.

links.passage:
Documented benefits include improved irrigation efficiency and reduced operator
exposure when spraying is done with strict SOPs (Miller et al., 2020).
supporting_passages:
UAV monitoring reduces scouting time and targets inputs, contributing to lower chemical and water use
while safeguarding yield.
links.inference_note: The preceding sentence names UAV monitoring as the technology whose documented benefits, including improved irrigation efficiency and lower water use, are then cited to Miller et al. (2020).
reference_entries: 33. Miller, P., et al. (2020). Drift Reduction Technologies for Aerial Spraying. Outlooks on Pest Management.
